title: Black Pepper

seo.title: Black Pepper (Maricha, Kali Mirch) - Benefits, Uses and Safety
seo.description: Learn about black pepper, or maricha, including its botanical identity, Ayurvedic properties, traditional uses for digestion and cough, dosage and safety considerations.

short_description: Black pepper is a pungent, heating spice traditionally used in small amounts to kindle Agni, reduce Kapha and support digestion, appetite and respiratory comfort.
full_description:
Black pepper is the dried fruit of Piper nigrum, known in Ayurveda as Maricha and in Hindi as kali mirch. It is one of the most widely used culinary spices and a classical Kapha-Vata pacifying dravya: katu (pungent), laghu (light), tikshna (sharp) and ushna (heating).

In traditional practice a pinch is used to stimulate digestion (dipana-pachana), reduce Ama and help clear sticky Kapha from the channels. Household uses include a pinch with honey for productive cough, and teas or decoctions with ginger and tulsi for seasonal congestion. It is also a component of Trikatu, the classical three-pungent combination of black pepper, long pepper and dry ginger. Culinary amounts in food are the usual starting point; concentrated powders and extracts should be used only with professional guidance.

recommended_dosage.decoction: A pinch in 30-50 ml warm tea or water
recommended_dosage.extract: Use only as directed by a qualified practitioner

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_effect: Traditionally considered balancing for Kapha and Vata; excess readily aggravates Pitta and may cause burning or heartburn.

key_benefits.benefit: Supports healthy digestion, appetite and Agni in small amounts.
May help reduce Ama and excess Kapha that feel heavy or sticky.
Traditionally used to ease productive cough and mild respiratory congestion.
Used as a yogavahi spice that may support the action of other herbs and foods.

therapeutic_uses.use: Traditionally used for Mandagni, indigestion, bloating and sluggish appetite.
Used for Kaphaja Kasa (wet cough), Pratishyaya and seasonal congestion, often with honey, ginger or tulsi.
Used in digestive and respiratory spice blends, including Trikatu.
Used in culinary amounts to flavour food and keep meals lighter and easier to digest.

safety_and_contraindications.safety: Use only small culinary amounts; excess can burn the throat, worsen reflux or aggravate Pitta.
People with ulcers, severe gastritis, bleeding disorders, or those taking medicines should consult a qualified healthcare professional before using concentrated pepper.
Keep pinches small for children; do not use bulk powder in infants, and seek advice in pregnancy before using it as a remedy.
Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction, severe burning or significant discomfort occurs.
